🎯 Today’s objective

By the end of this lesson I can...

✓ I can name 2-D shapes from their sides and angles

✓ I can find and draw lines of symmetry

✓ I can complete a shape using a line of symmetry

So you can design logos, badges and patios that look right!

🔑 Shape facts

Ask first, then click for each one.

🔺 3 sides

A shape with 3 sides is a ?

TRIANGLE

⬛ 4 sides

A shape with 4 sides is a ?

QUADRILATERAL (square, rectangle, kite, rhombus...)

⬠ 5, 6, 8

5, 6 and 8 sides are called ?

PENTAGON, HEXAGON, OCTAGON

📐 Right angle

A square corner is ?

a RIGHT ANGLE (90°)

✨ Regular

Regular means all sides are ?

EQUAL (and all angles equal)

Count the sides first. Then look at the corners.

Shape names: EASY

Q1

No calculator

[2 marks]

A drinks coaster is a regular hexagon. Write down the name of the shape. How many lines of symmetry does it have?

Hint

Answer

Count the sides. Regular: all sides equal.

Answer: Hexagon, 6 lines

click to solve →

Q2

No calculator

[2 marks]

A set square has 3 sides. Two sides are equal and it has 1 right angle. Write down the name of the shape. How many lines of symmetry does it have?

Hint

Answer

Count the sides, then look at the corners.

Answer: Right-angled triangle, 1 line

click to solve →

Q3

No calculator

[2 marks]

A window is a semicircle. How many straight sides does it have? How many lines of symmetry does it have?

Hint

Answer

Imagine folding it down the middle.

Answer: 1 straight side, 1 line

click to solve →

🏠 Menu

🔑 Symmetry facts

Ask first, then click for each one.

🪞 Line of symmetry

A line of symmetry is a ?

MIRROR line: fold it and both halves match

▭ Rectangle

A rectangle has ? lines

2 (NOT the diagonals)

⬛ Square

A square has ? lines

4 (2 straight, 2 diagonal)

✨ Regular shapes

A regular shape with 6 sides has ? lines

6 (same as the number of sides)

⚪ Circle

A circle has ? lines

INFINITE (any line through the middle)

Imagine folding it. Do both halves match?

🃏 True or false cards

TRUE or FALSE? Fix the false ones. Chat first, then click!

Card 1

A rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry.

✗ FALSE

2 lines. The diagonals do not work.

Card 2

A circle has no lines of symmetry.

✗ FALSE

It has infinite lines.

Card 3

An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry.

✔ TRUE

One from each corner.

Imagine the fold. Do BOTH halves match?

"When will I ever use this in real life?" Here is who uses it, every single day…

🎨

Graphic designers

Logos with lines of symmetry look balanced.

🧱

Tilers

Which shapes fit together on a floor?

🚗

Car designers

Both sides of a car are mirror images.

👗

Fashion designers

Cut one half, flip it for the other.

Count sides. Check corners. Fold to test symmetry.

🔤 Exam words

What does it mean? Ask first, then click for each one.

Line of symmetry

?

A fold line: both halves match.

A square has 4

Regular

?

All sides and angles equal.

A regular hexagon

Polygon

?

A flat shape with straight sides.

Triangle, hexagon

Parallel

?

Lines that never meet.

Opposite sides of a rectangle

Right angle

?

A square corner: 90°.

The corner of a page

Quadrilateral

?

Any 4-sided shape.

Square, kite, trapezium

Reflect

?

Flip over a mirror line.

Same distance, other side

Complete the shape

?

Draw the missing half.

Shade 7 more squares

Hexagon

?

6 sides.

A honeycomb cell

Octagon

?

8 sides.

A stop sign

🏠 Menu

Hard 1: mixed

Q1

Calculator

[5 marks]

Zak makes 20 stickers. Each sticker is a regular octagon with sides of 1.5 cm. Ribbon goes round the edge of each sticker. Ribbon is sold in 1 m rolls for £2.40. How much does the ribbon cost?

Hint

Answer

One sticker, then 20, then metres.

Answer: £7.20

click to solve →

Q2

Calculator

[5 marks]

A kite-shaped banner has one line of symmetry. Two sides are 1.2 m and two sides are 0.8 m. Trim goes all the way round. Jas makes 4 banners. Trim costs £3.25 per metre. She has £50. Is it enough?

Hint

Answer

Symmetry: the other sides match.

Answer: No, £52 (£2 short)

click to solve →

Q3

Calculator

[6 marks]

The patio has one line of symmetry. The cut-out is 3 m deep. Paving comes in packs that cover 10 m². How many packs are needed?

Hint

Answer

Use symmetry for the cut-out width.

Answer: 8 packs

click to solve →
